newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercials, CBOT soycomplex.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercials, CBOT soycomplex.

text.p: WCE canola ended higher on commercial demand and a jump in CBOT soy values, traders said.
"There was commercial and elevator company buying. Chicago was strong but there's a rumour crushers are bringing in European canola seed to crush because it's cheaper," a trader said.

March canola futures crush margin rose to -20.91 Tuesday from -24.55 Monday. March-May spread at $0.30, Mar-July at even money, Mar-Nov $43, May-Nov $42. Volume was 9,600 lots, or 192,000 tonnes, with 650 hedges.
Japan bought 3,000-4,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
March canola futures closed up $2.70 at $416.70 and May finished up $2.70 at $416.40.
March flax rose $1 to $352 and May climbed $2.60 to $353.60 on commercial demand. May-July spread at $1, Mar-May $1.30. Volume was 300 lots.

March western barley rose $0.90 to $139.90 on commission and commercial short covering with commission buy stops triggered in the March and October, October ended down $0.40 to $134. Mar-May spread at $0.50. Volume was 1,350 lots.
March feed wheat rose $1.70 to $171.70 and May rose $0.90 to $166.90 with Cargill selling to XCan, a trader said. Mar-July spread at $7.50. Volume was 730 lots.
Commercials bought 40 May feed pea contracts up US$2.50 at US$204 from commericals. Oats did not trade.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats and peas.)
